summary: gardener keeps main green in each onboarded repo: it watches the post-submit run on every main commit, publishes a tree status, groups failures by regression range, bisects them to a culprit and opens clean reverts within capped limits. It is the counterpart of Chromium's sheriff rotations, Sheriff-o-Matic and LUCI Bisection.

how_it_works.title: Tree status
how_it_works.text: For each repo the tree is closed while any post-submit builder's newest verdict is red, open when all are green, and unknown while a builder has no verdict yet. The tree-status workflow publishes status/<repo>.json and status/README.md to this repo's tree-status branch, committing only when something changes.

how_it_works.title: Coverage and backfill
how_it_works.text: Every main commit since a repo's first post-submit run must have a result, and a missing one fails the check. When a push of several commits ran only the newest, the cycle dispatches the post-submit workflow for each skipped commit, at most 10 in flight per repo.

how_it_works.title: Grouping and bisection
how_it_works.text: Red builders that share the same last-good to first-bad range form one failure group, typed as build, test, infra or unknown from the failed step names. qqgarden bisect binary-searches a range with a probe command, like git bisect run, and can verify the culprit by probing it and its parent again.

how_it_works.title: Capped reverts
how_it_works.text: Every cap comes from infra-config's auto_revert.toml at the pinned commit: at most daily_cap (10) reverts created per rolling 24 hours across all repos, plus per-type create and submit limits. A revert lands on its own only if the repo is in auto_land_repos; otherwise it is proposed as a PR, and infra and unknown failures are never reverted.

how_it_works.title: Ledger
how_it_works.text: Each revert is reserved as a write-once record on the ledger branch before its branch and PR exist, so a run that dies midway has still counted it. The cap counts only the gardener's own records.

key_files.what: Works out per-commit builder states and each repo's tree status.
Reads the revert caps and decides refuse, propose or land for each culprit.
The 5-minute gardening cycle: groups, verifies culprits and makes reverts.
Binary search for a culprit with a probe command.
Runs the status and cycle jobs and publishes to the tree-status and ledger branches.
The infra-config, test-pipelines and gate commits this repo reads.

try_it.note: The tests read infra-config at the commit pins.toml names, checked out under .qq/infra-config (tests/conftest.py).

status.text: Tree status is live: the tree-status branch holds status files for xo-space and innernet, and the workflow re-runs about every 5 minutes.
auto_land_repos is empty at the pinned infra-config commit, so every revert is only proposed and a person merges it. Test-failure reverts are proposed only in any case (submit limit 0).

Creating revert PRs, re-runs and backfills needs the gardener's own GitHub App; without it the cycle reports what it would do and creates nothing. Live reverts also wait on a manual ledger bootstrap and rulesets for the ledger and tree-status branches.
The tests need an infra-config checkout at the pins.toml commit in .qq/infra-config, or a path in QQ_INFRA_CONFIG.
